import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Convergence of fraction numerators $a(n)/b(n)$ to $e$

a: Numerators of a sequence of fractions converging to $e$.
$$a(1) = 3, a(2) = 5$$
For $n > 2$:
$$a(n) = \begin{cases} \left(\frac{n+2}{2}\right) a(n-1) - a(n-2) -
\left(\frac{n-2}{2}\right) a(n-3)
& \text{if } n \text{ is even} \cr 2 a(n-1) + n a(n-2) & \text{if } n \text{ is odd} \end{cases}$$

*References:*
- [A340737](https://oeis.org/A340737)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
- [b](https://oeis.org/b)
-/

namespace OeisA340737


open MeasureTheory

open scoped Real

open Nat

/--
Numerators of a sequence of fractions converging to $e$.
$$a(1) = 3, a(2) = 5$$
For $n > 2$:
$$a(n) = \begin{cases} \left(\frac{n+2}{2}\right) a(n-1) - a(n-2) -
\left(\frac{n-2}{2}\right) a(n-3)
& \text{if } n \text{ is even} \cr 2 a(n-1) + n a(n-2) & \text{if } n \text{ is odd} \end{cases}$$
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  match n with
  | 0 => 0 -- Required for total function, O(1,1) suggests 0 is not relevant.
  | 1 => 3
  | 2 => 5
  | n' + 3 => -- n $\ge$ 3
    let n := n' + 3

    let a_nm1 := a (n - 1)
    let a_nm2 := a (n - 2)
    let a_nm3 := a (n - 3)

    if n % 2 = 0 then
      -- n is even, n $\ge$ 4
      let c1 : ℕ := (n + 2) / 2
      let c2 : ℕ := (n - 2) / 2

      -- $a(n) = c_1 \cdot a(n-1) - a(n-2) - c_2 \cdot a(n-3)$.
      -- We use Int.ofNat for safe subtraction, as the result is known to be positive.
      Int.toNat (Int.ofNat c1 * Int.ofNat a_nm1 - Int.ofNat a_nm2 - Int.ofNat c2 * Int.ofNat a_nm3)
    else
      -- n is odd, n $\ge$ 3
      2 * a_nm1 + n * a_nm2
termination_by n

/--
Denominators of a sequence of fractions converging to $e$.
This sequence is defined by the same recurrence relation as a but with
initial values $b(1)=1, b(2)=2$.
$$b(1) = 1, b(2) = 2$$
For $n > 2$:
$$b(n) = \begin{cases} \left(\frac{n+2}{2}\right) b(n-1) - b(n-2) -
\left(\frac{n-2}{2}\right) b(n-3)
& \text{if } n \text{ is even} \cr 2 b(n-1) + n b(n-2) & \text{if } n \text{ is odd} \end{cases}$$
-/
def b (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  match n with
  | 0 => 0
  | 1 => 1
  | 2 => 2
  | n' + 3 => -- n $\ge$ 3
    let n := n' + 3

    let b_nm1 := b (n - 1)
    let b_nm2 := b (n - 2)
    let b_nm3 := b (n - 3)

    if n % 2 = 0 then
      -- n is even, n $\ge$ 4
      let c1 : ℕ := (n + 2) / 2
      let c2 : ℕ := (n - 2) / 2

      -- $b(n) = c_1 \cdot b(n-1) - b(n-2) - c_2 \cdot b(n-3)$.
      -- We use Int.ofNat for safe subtraction.
      Int.toNat (Int.ofNat c1 * Int.ofNat b_nm1 - Int.ofNat b_nm2 - Int.ofNat c2 * Int.ofNat b_nm3)
    else
      -- n is odd, n $\ge$ 3
      2 * b_nm1 + n * b_nm2
termination_by n


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_1 : a 1 = 3 := by unfold a; rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_2 : a 2 = 5 := by unfold a; rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_3 : a 3 = 19 := by unfold a; unfold a; unfold a; simp

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 49 := by unfold a; unfold a; unfold a; unfold a; simp

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_5 : a 5 = 193 := by unfold a; unfold a; unfold a; unfold a; unfold a; simp


/--
Conjecture: $\lim_{n \to \infty} a(n) / b(n) = e$, where $b(n)$ is the companion denominator sequence.

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/340737.wip.lean#L438"]
theorem tendsto_exp_one :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (a n : ℝ) / (b n : ℝ)) Filter.atTop (nhds (Real.exp 1)) := by
    sorry

end OeisA340737

findings.description: The module's companion-sequence reference is `[b](https://oeis.org/b)`, rather than a reference to A340738. OEIS explicitly identifies A340738 as the denominator sequence. This is only a reference slip: the definition `OeisA340737.b` has the correct initial values and recurrence.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A340737, cross-references: "Denominators are listed in A340738." A340738 gives initial values 1, 2 and exactly the recurrence used for `b`. Full entries read through the official mirror: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A340/A340737.seq and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A340/A340738.seq.

reformulations.difference: The limit uses total natural-valued sequences, with `Int.toNat` in the even recurrence and `a 0 = b 0 = 0`. OEIS specifies positive-index sequences using ordinary subtraction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Both sequences are strictly increasing and positive for n ≥ 1. At an even index n = 2k ≥ 4, write X = x(n−1), Y = x(n−2), Z = x(n−3). The signed recurrence value is (k+1)X−Y−(k−1)Z ≥ 2X−Y > X > 0, so `Int.toNat` never clips it. Both divisions by 2 are exact at even indices. Lean proofs in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean establish equality with untruncated integer recurrences and an explicit equivalence of the limit statements, without using the conjecture. No positive-index term depends on the value at zero: the n=3 branch uses only indices 1 and 2, and subsequent relevant indices are positive. The shift equivalence proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean shows that including the initial 0/0 value does not affect convergence.

sources_consulted: Tsoukalas et al., Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search, arXiv:2605.22763v2, OEIS discussion; abstract and LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763 and https://arxiv.org/e-print/2605.22763

Adamczewski, OEIS Open: How many conjectures can language models turn into theorems?, arXiv:2608.11941v2, Appendix A, A340738 entry; abstract and LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11941 and https://arxiv.org/e-print/2608.11941
review.notes: All eight declarations were checked: the two definitions, five initial-value lemmas, and limit theorem. No mathematical misformalization was found. Lean evaluated the sequences through n=15 and verified the boundary and limit-equivalence checks. An independent signed big-integer computation matched all 730 numerator-table entries and all 731 denominator-table entries. The solved status is consistent with A340737's June 9, 2026 comment recording a proof, the cited paper's published proof artifact, and the later A340738 proof summary. Direct OEIS entry requests were blocked by Cloudflare; their complete entries were read through OEIS's official data mirror.
